# Saturated-conductivity PTFs for temperate and tropical soils.

## Source

Ottoni, M. V., Ottoni Filho, T. B., Lopes-Assad, M. L. R. C., & Rotunno Filho, O. C. (2019). Pedotransfer functions for saturated hydraulic conductivity using a database with temperate and tropical climate soils. Journal of Hydrology, 575, 1345-1358.

[DOI: 10.1016/j.jhydrol.2019.05.050](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jhydrol.2019.05.050)

## Scope

**Territory:** Brazil and Europe.

**Dataset:** Balanced 824-sample study set selected from 412 Brazilian HYBRAS samples and 1077 European HYPRES samples: 425 calibration samples (215 Brazilian and 210 European) and 399 validation samples (197 Brazilian and 202 European).

## Functions

### `calc_ptf_ottoni2019_wm330`

Estimate saturated hydraulic conductivity from effective porosity.

**Status:** `implemented`

**Prediction target:** Saturated hydraulic conductivity from measured effective porosity.

**Models:** $k(h)$ — Saturated hydraulic conductivity

#### Inputs

| Name | Type | Unit | Domain | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `effective_porosity` | `number` | cm^3/cm^3 | Calibration range 0.012-0.458; validation range 0.016-0.405. | Effective porosity, defined as total porosity minus volumetric water content at 330 cm suction. |

#### Outputs

| Name | Unit | Domain | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `k_sat` | cm/day | value >= 0 | Saturated hydraulic conductivity. |

!!! note

    Effective porosity is total porosity minus water content at 330 cm suction. Callers supply that preprocessed predictor directly.

!!! warning

    When total porosity was unavailable, the study used saturated water content; when theta_330 was unavailable, it selected the closest measurement between 300 and 350 cm suction. This API does not perform those data-dependent substitutions.

### `calc_ptf_ottoni2019_wmssc`

Estimate saturated hydraulic conductivity from silt and clay.

**Status:** `implemented`

**Prediction target:** Saturated hydraulic conductivity from silt and clay contents.

**Models:** $k(h)$ — Saturated hydraulic conductivity

#### Inputs

| Name | Type | Unit | Domain | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `silt` | `number` | % | Calibration range 0.0-81.7%; validation range 0.0-78.9%. | Silt content by mass using the source's common USDA/FAO limits. |
| `clay` | `number` | % | Calibration range 0.0-96.0%; validation range 0.0-93.0%. | Clay content by mass using the source's common USDA/FAO limits. |

#### Outputs

| Name | Unit | Domain | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `k_sat` | cm/day | value > 0 | Saturated hydraulic conductivity. |

!!! note

    The printed linear equation predicts the base-10 logarithm of Ks.

!!! warning

    Published predictor ranges are marginal sample summaries, not clipping bounds or a Cartesian applicability domain.

### `calc_ptf_ottoni2019_wmf330`

Estimate saturated hydraulic conductivity from silt, clay and bulk density through estimated effective porosity.

**Status:** `blocked`

**Prediction target:** Saturated hydraulic conductivity from estimated effective porosity.

**Models:** $k(h)$ — Saturated hydraulic conductivity

#### Inputs

| Name | Type | Unit | Domain | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `silt` | `number` | % | Calibration range 0.0-81.7%; validation range 0.0-78.9%. | Silt content by mass using the source's common USDA/FAO limits. |
| `clay` | `number` | % | Calibration range 0.0-96.0%; validation range 0.0-93.0%. | Clay content by mass using the source's common USDA/FAO limits. |

#### Outputs

| Name | Unit | Domain | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `k_sat` | cm/day | value >= 0 when estimated effective porosity is non-negative | Saturated hydraulic conductivity. |

!!! note

    The final-article coefficient is 1266; the supplied evidence identifies 51.1 as a conflicting earlier secondary-source value.

!!! warning

    Blocked pending a source-supported joint applicability domain or a defined policy for zero or negative estimated effective porosity.

!!! warning

    Published predictor ranges are marginal sample summaries. Some combinations within their Cartesian product make estimated effective porosity negative, for which the fractional power is not real-valued.
